holidays.name: National Wienerschnitzel Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the crispy, golden breaded cutlet, or to cheerfully argue about whether the hot dog chain of a similar name counts. Break out the lemon wedges and mallets.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance in the US that borrows from the classic Austrian dish. Wiener Schnitzel has been a Viennese staple for centuries, and its legal definition in Austria requires it to be made from veal.
holidays.funFact: In Austria, a schnitzel labeled 'Wiener Schnitzel' must legally be made from veal. If it's made from pork, it must be called 'Wiener Schnitzel vom Schwein'.

holidays.name: International Day to Protect Education from Attack
holidays.description: A serious observance, but an important one. It draws attention to the need to protect students, teachers, and schools in conflict zones.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2020 and first observed on September 9, 2021, to highlight attacks on education worldwide.
holidays.funFact: The day was proposed by Qatar and backed by dozens of countries, and it is observed annually by UNESCO and UNICEF.

holidays.name: Teddy Bear Day
holidays.description: A cuddly day to hug your favorite stuffed bear, give one as a gift, or finally admit that your childhood teddy still sleeps on your bed.
holidays.origin: Teddy bears are named after US President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt, who refused to shoot a captured bear on a 1902 hunting trip. A cartoon of the event inspired toymakers to create the 'Teddy's bear.' The September 9 observance is an informal celebration of that legacy.
holidays.funFact: The first teddy bears were made in 1902-1903 by Morris Michtom in Brooklyn, who got Roosevelt's permission to use his name.

holidays.name: National Steak au Poivre Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy a peppercorn-crusted steak, usually served with a creamy cognac sauce. It's fancy enough for a candlelit dinner and easy enough to cook at home.
holidays.origin: A food observance celebrating the French bistro classic whose name means 'steak with pepper.' It has been a restaurant favorite since the early 20th century.
holidays.funFact: Traditional steak au poivre is often flambéed with cognac at the table, which has made for some very dramatic and occasionally eyebrow-singeing dinners.

holidays.name: Google Doodle Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the creative logo changes that Google has been making to mark holidays, anniversaries, and celebrations around the world.
holidays.origin: The very first Google Doodle appeared in 1998, when founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin put a stick figure behind the second 'o' to signal they were out of the office at Burning Man. The anniversary of Google's founding is celebrated in September, and some fans mark Doodle appreciation around this time.
holidays.funFact: Google has created thousands of doodles since 1998, and some are fully playable games, like the 2010 interactive Pac-Man doodle.
